metadata.title: Prevention and Treatment of Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy: Developing Drug and Biological Products in Oncology
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 23 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 24 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 25 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 26 not required. 27
candidates.context: This guidance provides recommendations to sponsors for the clinical development of drug and 17 biological products 2 intended for the prevention and treatment of chemotherapy-induced 18 peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) in oncology patient populations. The guidance pertains to 19 development programs for drugs regulated by the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research and 20 the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research. 21

candidates.statement: — If no clinical data exist on the effect of the investigational drug in patients with 69 cancer, initial clinical investigations of the CIPN investigational drug should 70 include only participants with unresectable or metastatic (incurable) cancer. 71 Patients with early-stage (curable) cancer should not be included in the initial 72 clinical investigation as any impact on the efficacy of cancer treatment could 73 compromise a patient’s chance for cure. 74

candidates.statement: — As with all FDA-regulated clinical trials, investigators must obtain informed 82 consent from each participant (or their legally authorized representative) in 83 accordance with 21 CFR part 50 prior to their enrollment in a CIPN trial. Among 84 other information, participants must be informed of “any reasonably foreseeable 85 risks” as part of the informed consent process. 5 Regardless of the cancer stage of 86 the potential CIPN trial participant, this would generally include the possible risk 87 that the investigational drug may worsen their cancer either through interference 88 with cancer treatment or promotion of tumor growth. 89
candidates.context: — If nonclinical data and initial clinical data in participants with unresectable or 76 metastatic (incurable) cancer for the CIPN investigational drug do not show a 77 potential interaction with cancer treatment or promotion of tumor growth, 78 subsequent trials of the CIPN drug may occur in participants with early-stage 79 (curable) disease, with appropriate justification. 80 • CIPN trials should be randomized to compare participants receiving the CIPN 91 investigational drug to a control group to assess whether the treatment effect is 92 attributable to the CIPN drug rather than the natural history of CIPN. CIPN may improve 93 without intervention after chemotherapy is withdrawn, although improvement is less 94 likely for patients with persistent CIPN long after completing chemotherapy. 95

candidates.statement: • FDA has no defined set of recommended clinical outcome measures to assess efficacy for 114 trials intended to support approval of drugs for the prevention or treatment of CIPN. 115 Patient-reported outcomes, clinician-reported outcomes, or objective measures of patient 116 function that measure symptoms or functions relevant to CIPN may be considered as 117 efficacy endpoints. The selection of appropriate efficacy endpoints should consider the 118 manifestations of CIPN that the investigational drug is anticipated to impact (e.g., 119

sensory, motor or autonomic deficits) and whether the investigational drug is intended to 120 show benefit on existing symptoms of CIPN or prevent the development of CIPN. 121 Sponsors should consult FDA early in the process of the selection and/or development of 122 efficacy endpoints for CIPN. 123
candidates.context: • A standardized assessment of dosage modifications due to peripheral neuropathy could 125 be a secondary endpoint. Ideally, effective CIPN drugs would minimize chemotherapy 126 dosage interruptions, dose reductions, and drug discontinuations. 127

candidates.statement: • For a trial intended to support a marketing application, oncology-specific endpoints to 129 assess the efficacy of cancer treatments should be included as secondary endpoints to 130 evaluate the potential interference with cancer treatment or the promotion of tumor 131 growth by the CIPN drug. 132

Ideally, effective CIPN drugs would minimize chemotherapy 126 dosage interruptions, dose reductions, and drug discontinuations. 127 — In the metastatic cancer setting, these endpoints may include overall response 134 rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival (OS). 135

candidates.statement: • For a trial intended to support a marketing application, the oncology-specific endpoint(s) 140 should be included as part of the statistical hierarchy and evaluated with appropriate 141 alpha allocation. While it may not be feasible to adequately power for oncology-specific 142 endpoint(s) in CIPN trials, it will be important to evaluate whether the oncology-specific 143 endpoint(s) at the time of the primary analysis shows a detrimental effect of the CIPN 144 drug. 145
candidates.context: — In the early-stage setting, these endpoints may include disease-free survival, 137 event-free survival, and OS. 138 — A plan for long-term follow-up should be pre-specified and allow for sufficient 147 maturity to evaluate whether the oncology-specific endpoint(s) shows a 148 detrimental effect of the CIPN drug. A formal interim analysis of oncology- 149 specific endpoint(s) should be conducted at the time of the CIPN primary efficacy 150 analysis. The plan for long-term follow-up should be discussed with the Agency 151 prior to initiation. 152
